Take a look at issues 43 and 44.  Now that we have some more GL hacks ported, it's probably a good time to investigate more approaches that could improve the performance.

I'm about to go to bed, so I won't be here to approve any decisions or let you flash the device for a few hours.  So try and make as much progress as you can, leaving comments on the issues, and put together a report of things you tried, what you learned, and what you want to do next.  I'll probably be back around 7am.

#43 Speed up TinyGL's vertex and triangle setup on the S3 [open]
TinyGL on the S3 spends about 6 us per vertex on setup, which is why GL hacks
run at 4 to 9 fps. Find out why and cut it. Measured on the spike branch
`worktree-spike-tinygl` (see `docs/tinygl-spike.md` there); depends on #42.

## Measurements

Gears with a fixed seed (a planetary set with a big ring), 466 by 466,
single-precision TinyGL, one light, a frame is 17,706 vertices and 17,620
triangles:

| Part of the frame | Time |
| --- | --- |
| Clear (colour and z, both in PSRAM) | 24.6 ms |
| Fill (a quarter-size viewport saved 30 to 35 ms) | about 40 ms |
| Vertex and triangle setup | about 100 to 120 ms |
| Push to the display (existing) | 32 ms |

Light Gears layouts (about 4,300 vertices) run at about 9 fps. Pipes probe
numbers: 3.7 ms for a 544-vertex lit sphere, about 4 us per vertex before
lighting and about 2.8 us more with it.

## Tried, and made no difference

- `-O2` instead of `-Os` for the TinyGL files (about 1 percent). Building the
  whole firmware at `-O2` crashes the compiler in `braid_single.c`.
- Specular lookup tables (`TGL_FEATURE_SPECULAR_BUFFERS`) instead of `pow`
  (needs a one-line prototype fix in `zgl.h`): no change.
- Wireframe mode: no change, because the wire sphere sends twice the vertices.

## Ideas, none tried

- Float divides are software on the S3's FPU. TinyGL's triangle setup divides
  several times per triangle. Replace with a reciprocal and multiplies, or
  fixed point. Profile first (a temporary early return in `gl_draw_triangle`,
  as the repo does for Braid).
- Put the hot vertex and triangle functions in IRAM, if flash cache misses
  turn out to matter.
- Use the second core (core 0 is mostly idle) for part of the pipeline.
- Cheaper clear: 24.6 ms for 868 KB is PSRAM write speed. A smaller or
  narrower z-buffer, or clearing only the dirty rows, might help.
- Prefer lighter Gears layouts through a `HackEntry` override, as Galaxy does
  with `count: -3`. Trades variety for speed.
- Render at a reduced size and let the push scale (changes what the push
  does, so needs a discussion).

## How to measure

`glshim.c` on the spike branch logs `GL frames= verts/frame= tris/frame=
clear= gl=` every 5 seconds. `-DGL_SPIKE_SEED=7` makes the scene repeatable
(try seeds 5 for one gear, 7 for the heavy planetary set).


--- comment:
Notes from landing Gears (PR #47). Posted by Claude, an agent working under Rod's direction.

## What landed, so you know the starting point

- TinyGL is patched at build time by `tools/tinygl_patch.py`; the GL layer is `firmware/src/glshim/`. The gotchas are in `.claude/rules/gl.md`.
- The spike's `GL frames=` log line and `-DGL_SPIKE_SEED` did not come across to main. Measure with the `run Gears fps= step= push=` line instead, or bring the spike logging back.
- Gears on the device, 48 restarts with random layouts: 2.8 to 10.0 fps, step 65 to 330 ms, push about 34 ms, wait 0. The first layout after each boot is always the same (`random()` is seeded the same way), so reboots do not sample layouts.

## Things to know before optimising

- **Specular is off by default.** TinyGL sets `zEnableSpecular = 0` unless the application calls `glSetEnableSpecular(1)`, so Gears has no highlights today and `glMateriali` has no visible effect. Turning it on is a fidelity-versus-speed decision that belongs in this issue. The shim test for `glMateriali` calls `glSetEnableSpecular(1)` for this reason.
- **Software `double` is still in the lighting and clip path.** After the single-precision patch, `gl_clipcode` and `gl_shade_vertex` still call `double` helpers: `CLIP_EPSILON` is an exponent literal, which `tools/float_literals.py` leaves alone. That is a likely contributor to the 6 us per vertex, and it is cheap to try first.
- **Every frame is a full-canvas push.** Gears dirties all 466 rows (`rows=466`), so push cost is fixed at about 32 to 34 ms regardless of layout. Anything that lets the push send fewer rows would need the dirty rectangle to be tighter than the whole canvas.
- **Clear is 24.6 ms of the frame.** TinyGL clears colour and z every frame. The z-buffer is 434 KB in PSRAM.
- **Host timing does not predict the board.** Gears costs a lot on the host too: it adds about 14 s to `test_push_present` (3,000 full pushes). Do not use the host probe to rank GL changes.

## Smaller leads

- The vertex-array shim expands `glDrawArrays` into immediate `glVertex3f` calls (`glshim.c`). Display lists recorded this way carry the expanded vertices, so any change to how lists store geometry will touch it.
- Gears' light layouts have about 4,300 vertices and its heavy ones about 17,700, so any speed-up shows most on the heavy layouts. `*cycles` and `*ncolors` are overridden to 0 and 64 in `registry.c`.
- Upstream `free_gears` leaks `bp->gears` (36 to 1,620 B of internal heap per start; about 14 KB over 48 restarts). Not a speed issue, but it will show up in any long restart test.


--- comment:
Status update from Claude (an agent working under Rod's direction), as of the end of the 2026-10-09/10 session. Everything below is on `main`.

## What landed

- **#51, clip epsilon.** `CLIP_EPSILON` was `1E-5`, a double, so `gl_clipcode` ran a software double multiply on every vertex. It is now `1E-5f`. On the board, CubicGrid's step (8,000 unlit points, a deterministic boot) fell by a flat 5.6 ms in every window (about 11 percent, 0.7 us a vertex); Morph3D by about 3 ms. Frame hashes are unchanged.
- **#52, dirty rectangle.** TinyGL reports the box around everything it draws. `glClear` clears only the box drawn since the last clear and a swap marks only what was drawn and what the clear erased, so the push sends those rows. A new context and a new clear colour are full clears. Morph3D's step fell from 75 to 83 ms to 55 to 59 and its push from 32.5 ms to 2 to 9 (91 to 192 rows of 466); Gears' first layout step from 65 to 79 ms to 44 to 63 and push from 32 to 34 to 4 to 12. CubicGrid pays about 1 ms for the bookkeeping and gains nothing, as its points cover the whole screen.
- **The hacks' own pauses.** The work shrank, but the frame rate barely moved, because each hack asks for a pause after every frame and the loop credits only the push against it. Morph3D (40 ms) and Gears (30 ms) now register `*delay: 10000`. Result: Morph3D 8.4 fps at the start of the evening to 14.4 to 15.2; Gears' first layout 9.0 to 10.2 to 12.6 to 17.6 (about 14.5 on average). A heavy Gears layout is render-bound and gains little.

Tests: pinned frame hashes are unchanged for every hack, so output is pixel-identical, and the shadow-display replay passes. The review on #52 found five issues (one real bug: right-to-left lines left stale pixels); all are fixed and tested.

## Where a frame goes (CubicGrid, 8,000 points, 46.7 ms step)

Measured with temporary early returns in TinyGL, never committed. Colour clear 12.7 ms (27 percent, about 34 MB/s, so memory bandwidth); vertex pipeline 13.3 ms (28 percent, about 1.7 us a vertex); drawing the points 11.1 ms (24 percent, about 1.4 us a point); list read and dispatch about 9.6 ms (21 percent; the cause is my guess, probably PSRAM reads). Details and the dirty-rectangle numbers are in `docs/gl-budget.md`.

## Checked and ruled out

- **Software `double` in lighting.** After #51 the only soft-double references left in TinyGL are per call (`glFrustum`, `glopLight`, `glopRotate`, `glClearDepth`, a debug printer), plus two `1E-3` compares in `gl_shade_vertex` that run only for positional lights and specular. Gears and Morph3D use directional lights with specular off, so they never run; I did not patch them without a hack to time.
- **Skipping the z clear.** CubicGrid clears colour only, and Gears and Morph3D need depth.
- **Host timing** still does not predict the board; the harness (`tools/gl_budget.py`) counts work and predicted frame times to about 10 percent before the dirty rectangle, but its clear and push constants now overstate sparse hacks and need a refit.

## Ideas from the first list, and where they stand

- Float divides in triangle setup: not measured.
- IRAM for the hot functions, and using core 0: not tried.
- Cheaper clear: done for sparse scenes by the dirty rectangle.
- Lighter Gears layouts through an override: not done (the pause change helped the light ones; the heavy ones are still 3 to 5 fps).
- Render at a reduced size: not done.
- **New:** overlap the push with the next frame (core 0 pushes, core 1 renders), which could take a frame from step plus push to the larger of the two. It needs a second 434 KB buffer and a lock around M5GFX, and PSRAM bandwidth may limit the gain. Untried.

## Open decisions and gaps

- Specular is still off (fidelity versus speed); not decided.
- Only Gears' first layout after boot was timed with the dirty rectangle, not the heavy layouts; nobody has run the new build for long.
- Morph3D's two middle shapes have never appeared on the board, and CubicGrid has had no long run: #50.


--- comment:
Correction to my status comment above, from Claude (an agent working under Rod's direction).

I wrote that the harness (`tools/gl_budget.py`) "counts work and predicted frame times to about 10 percent before the dirty rectangle". That holds for Gears and CubicGrid but **not for Morph3D**, which the model under-predicted by 11 to 20 percent.

What went wrong: I had matched Morph3D's earlier measured steps to its shapes by size alone, and matched them to the wrong ones. Morph3D has five shapes (2,300, 3,864, 5,040, 5,100 and 7,200 vertices), not four. An overnight capture on the final code (2h13m, 795 rotations, no resets) showed four step clusters (about 21, 40, 55 and 74 ms), and the earlier 48 ms and 78 to 82 ms steps were the 2,300 and the 5,040 or 5,100 vertex shapes. The cause of the error is the first worry from the review: Morph3D has two lights and the model charged one lighting cost per lit vertex.

The fix is in #53: the harness now counts a light term for each enabled light, which reproduces all five shapes (predicted old steps of 48, 66, 80 or 82 and 102 ms against 48 and 78 to 82 measured directly and about 45, 65, 81 and 102 inferred). The same capture found no PSRAM leak, and attributes the internal heap drift (about 388 bytes a lap) to Gears' known upstream leak rather than to Morph3D or CubicGrid.

Nothing in the optimisation numbers above changes; this is about the harness's accuracy, not the speed-ups. Until #53 merges, `docs/gl-budget.md` on `main` still has the wrong Morph3D rows.


#44 Pipes on TinyGL: too slow as written, and what would change that [open]
Pipes was the first GL hack tried and it is not viable on TinyGL as written.
Record what was learned and what would change that. Depends on #42; see also
#43. Data is in `docs/tinygl-spike.md` on branch `worktree-spike-tinygl`.

## Why it is slow

Pipes does not accumulate. Every frame it clears and redraws every piece so
far from display lists (`draw_pipes` loops over `system_index`), up to about
500 pieces per system with the defaults, under a slowly rotating camera. Cost
grows with the pipe, and every frame changes completely, so pushing only the
changed rows saves nothing.

With Pipes' real primitives (triangle-strip spheres of 16 by 16, 24-facet
quad-strip tubes), measured on the S3 at 464 by 464:

- 3.7 ms per piece, plus about 80 ms fixed per frame.
- 2.8 fps at 80 pieces, 1.2 fps at 210, under 1 fps by 250.
- Wireframe (`*wireframe: True`) is no faster: the same frame times, because
  the cost is per vertex and the wire sphere sends twice the vertices.
- 8 by 8 spheres (about 3.7 times fewer triangles) gave 5.2 fps at 50 pieces,
  3.4 at 100. Not enough on its own.

## What would change that

- Stop redrawing the settled scene. The camera turns only 0.02 degrees per
  frame, so drawing just the newest piece onto the existing frame, and
  redrawing everything only now and then, would make the cost per frame
  constant. Needs interception at the GL layer and slightly changes the look
  (the older pieces lag the camera).
- Faster vertex setup in TinyGL (#43).

## Port notes

- The real spheres come from `unit_sphere` in `sphere.c`, which builds
  `glVertexPointer` arrays and calls `glDrawArrays` inside a display list.
  TinyGL gets that wrong; the array shim from #42 fixes it.
- Pipes also needs `buildlwo.c`, `teapot.c` (built unconditionally),
  `sphere.c`, `gltrackball.c` and `rotator.c`. All are in `hacks/glx/`, so
  they can be copied byte-identical.
- Pipes uses two lights' state and a specular material.


#45 Choose the next GL hacks after Gears (survey of 146, nothing measured yet) [closed]
Which GL hacks to try after Gears (#42). This is a static survey of the
xscreensaver 6.16 sources; nothing here is measured on the device.

## What the scan looked at

All 146 GL hacks in `hacks/glx/`, flagging use of features TinyGL lacks or
handles poorly:

| Feature | Hacks using it |
| --- | --- |
| Textures | 87 |
| Blending (`GL_BLEND`, `glBlendFunc`) | 84 |
| Fog | 17 |
| Stencil | 2 |
| Pixel read-back or copy | 4 |
| Accumulation buffer | 0 |

TinyGL's blending ignores alpha, so blend-only hacks may degrade rather than
fail. Only 36 hacks are clear of all six.

## Clear of all six

`stonerview`, `sproingiewrap`, `swim`, `b_lockglue`, `dangerball`,
`moebiusgears`, `glknots`, `covid19`, `hilbert`, `bubble3d`, `sierpinski3d`,
`splodesic`, `cubicgrid`, `hexstrut`, `pipes`, `kallisti`, `cubestorm`,
`cubetwist`, `morph3d`, `superquadrics`, `surfaces`, `voronoi`, `hextrail`,
`menger`, `topblock`, `gears`, `razzledazzle`, `cityflow`, `sproingies`,
`companion`, `rubik`, `shark`, `whale`, `dolphin`, `gltext`.

Blend only (no textures, fog, stencil or read-back): `antinspect`, `beats`,
`blinkbox`, `boing`, `crackberg`, `crumbler`, `cubestack`, `deepstars`,
`geodesic`, `hydrostat`, `hypertorus`, `hypnowheel`, `kaleidocycle`,
`lockward`, `nakagin`, `polytopes`, `tronbit`, `unknownpleasures`.

## Shortlist, and why

Speed is roughly 6 us per lit vertex plus about 80 ms fixed per frame (#43),
so the question is vertices per frame, not features. Estimates only:

- `morph3d`: morphing lit polyhedra, no growth. Probably small.
- `stonerview`: 155 lines, no lighting or textures.
- `kallisti`: small and lit. Read it first.
- `gears`: done in #42.

Probably too heavy: `superquadrics` (25 objects at up to 50 by 50),
`moebiusgears` (17 gears), `glknots` (800 segments), `dangerball` (a 32-slice
sphere with spikes), `cubestorm` (snakes of 200 cubes), `menger`,
`pipes` (#44).

## Suggested next step

Measure instead of guessing. The spike already counts vertices and triangles
per frame inside TinyGL. A host harness that runs a hack against it would
give a polygon budget for each candidate without a flash. Once the GL layer
from #42 is in, that harness is a small step.

Features TinyGL lacks that other hacks will hit: `glTexGeni`, `glFog*`,
`glInterleavedArrays` (see the Flying Toasters issue).

130	#43. Data is in `docs/tinygl-spike.md` on branch `worktree-spike-tinygl`.
131	
132	## Why it is slow
133	
134	Pipes does not accumulate. Every frame it clears and redraws every piece so
135	far from display lists (`draw_pipes` loops over `system_index`), up to about
136	500 pieces per system with the defaults, under a slowly rotating camera. Cost
137	grows with the pipe, and every frame changes completely, so pushing only the
138	changed rows saves nothing.
139	
140	With Pipes' real primitives (triangle-strip spheres of 16 by 16, 24-facet
141	quad-strip tubes), measured on the S3 at 464 by 464:
142	
143	- 3.7 ms per piece, plus about 80 ms fixed per frame.
144	- 2.8 fps at 80 pieces, 1.2 fps at 210, under 1 fps by 250.
145	- Wireframe (`*wireframe: True`) is no faster: the same frame times, because
146	  the cost is per vertex and the wire sphere sends twice the vertices.
147	- 8 by 8 spheres (about 3.7 times fewer triangles) gave 5.2 fps at 50 pieces,
148	  3.4 at 100. Not enough on its own.
149	
150	## What would change that
151	
152	- Stop redrawing the settled scene. The camera turns only 0.02 degrees per
153	  frame, so drawing just the newest piece onto the existing frame, and
154	  redrawing everything only now and then, would make the cost per frame
155	  constant. Needs interception at the GL layer and slightly changes the look
156	  (the older pieces lag the camera).
157	- Faster vertex setup in TinyGL (#43).
158	
159	## Port notes
160	
161	- The real spheres come from `unit_sphere` in `sphere.c`, which builds
162	  `glVertexPointer` arrays and calls `glDrawArrays` inside a display list.
163	  TinyGL gets that wrong; the array shim from #42 fixes it.
164	- Pipes also needs `buildlwo.c`, `teapot.c` (built unconditionally),
165	  `sphere.c`, `gltrackball.c` and `rotator.c`. All are in `hacks/glx/`, so
166	  they can be copied byte-identical.
167	- Pipes uses two lights' state and a specular material.
168	
169	
170	#45 Choose the next GL hacks after Gears (survey of 146, nothing measured yet) [closed]
171	Which GL hacks to try after Gears (#42). This is a static survey of the
172	xscreensaver 6.16 sources; nothing here is measured on the device.
173	
174	## What the scan looked at
175	
176	All 146 GL hacks in `hacks/glx/`, flagging use of features TinyGL lacks or
177	handles poorly:
178	
179	| Feature | Hacks using it |
180	| --- | --- |
181	| Textures | 87 |
182	| Blending (`GL_BLEND`, `glBlendFunc`) | 84 |
183	| Fog | 17 |
184	| Stencil | 2 |
185	| Pixel read-back or copy | 4 |
186	| Accumulation buffer | 0 |
187	
188	TinyGL's blending ignores alpha, so blend-only hacks may degrade rather than
189	fail. Only 36 hacks are clear of all six.
190	
191	## Clear of all six
192	
193	`stonerview`, `sproingiewrap`, `swim`, `b_lockglue`, `dangerball`,
194	`moebiusgears`, `glknots`, `covid19`, `hilbert`, `bubble3d`, `sierpinski3d`,
195	`splodesic`, `cubicgrid`, `hexstrut`, `pipes`, `kallisti`, `cubestorm`,
196	`cubetwist`, `morph3d`, `superquadrics`, `surfaces`, `voronoi`, `hextrail`,
197	`menger`, `topblock`, `gears`, `razzledazzle`, `cityflow`, `sproingies`,
198	`companion`, `rubik`, `shark`, `whale`, `dolphin`, `gltext`.
199	
200	Blend only (no textures, fog, stencil or read-back): `antinspect`, `beats`,
201	`blinkbox`, `boing`, `crackberg`, `crumbler`, `cubestack`, `deepstars`,
202	`geodesic`, `hydrostat`, `hypertorus`, `hypnowheel`, `kaleidocycle`,
203	`lockward`, `nakagin`, `polytopes`, `tronbit`, `unknownpleasures`.
204	
205	## Shortlist, and why
206	
207	Speed is roughly 6 us per lit vertex plus about 80 ms fixed per frame (#43),
208	so the question is vertices per frame, not features. Estimates only:
209	
210	- `morph3d`: morphing lit polyhedra, no growth. Probably small.
211	- `stonerview`: 155 lines, no lighting or textures.
212	- `kallisti`: small and lit. Read it first.
213	- `gears`: done in #42.
214	
215	Probably too heavy: `superquadrics` (25 objects at up to 50 by 50),
216	`moebiusgears` (17 gears), `glknots` (800 segments), `dangerball` (a 32-slice
217	sphere with spikes), `cubestorm` (snakes of 200 cubes), `menger`,
218	`pipes` (#44).
219	
220	## Suggested next step
221	
222	Measure instead of guessing. The spike already counts vertices and triangles
223	per frame inside TinyGL. A host harness that runs a hack against it would
224	give a polygon budget for each candidate without a flash. Once the GL layer
225	from #42 is in, that harness is a small step.
226	
227	Features TinyGL lacks that other hacks will hit: `glTexGeni`, `glFog*`,
228	`glInterleavedArrays` (see the Flying Toasters issue).
229	
230	
231	--- comment:
232	Written by Claude (an agent working for Rod), closing this out.
233	
234	This issue asked which GL hacks to try after Gears, and suggested measuring
235	instead of guessing. That is what happened.
236	
237	## What was done
238	
239	- **A host tool to measure instead of guess:** `tools/gl_budget.py` (on `main`,
240	  documented in `docs/gl-budget.md`). It runs a GL hack on the host through a
241	  private, instrumented copy of TinyGL, counts vertices, triangles, points and
242	  filled pixels per frame, and predicts the device frame time with the #43 cost
243	  model. The fill cost is fitted to one Gears scene.
244	- **Two ports picked with it:** Morph3D is merged (#48) and CubicGrid is in a
245	  draft PR (#49). Both run unmodified source behind a `USE_GL` wrapper.
246	- **A TinyGL bug the Morph3D port found:** `glLightModelfv` always copied four
247	  floats, so a one-element argument read past the array. Fixed in
248	  `tools/tinygl_patch.py`, with a test.
249	- **Where the survey was wrong:** `stonerview` was listed as clear of blending
250	  but calls `glBlendFunc` and `glHint`, and its sources total 762 lines, not
251	  155. `cubicgrid` was not on the shortlist but turned out to have almost no
252	  shim work, because its helpers were already in the GL layer.
253	
254	## How accurate the tool was
255	
256	Predicted against measured on the board, as step plus push:
257	
258	| Scene | Predicted | Measured |
259	| --- | --- | --- |
260	| Morph3D, heavy shape | 114 ms | 111 to 118 ms |
261	| Morph3D, light shape | 87 ms | 84 ms |
262	| CubicGrid, 27,000 points | 165 ms | 170 to 180 ms |
263	| CubicGrid, 8,000 points | 89 ms | 80 to 88 ms |
264	
265	Good to about 10 percent on scenes not used in the fit, and it ranked them
266	correctly. Review had warned it might be optimistic for Morph3D (two lights,
267	tiny triangles) and for CubicGrid (uncosted, wide points); neither showed up.
268	`docs/gl-budget.md` has the full table and its limits.
269	
270	CubicGrid at its default grid (27,000 points) ran at 5.6 to 6 fps, which Rod
271	found too slow, so it is registered with `*ticks: 20` and runs at 11 to 12 fps.
272	Rod judged that the better look on the small display too.
273	
274	## What is left
275	
276	- Morph3D's two middle shapes have not appeared on the board, and CubicGrid has
277	  not had a long rotating capture: tracked in #50.
278	- The remaining candidates here are untried. `kallisti` needs the `gllist`
279	  helper, which the GL layer does not have; the harness can price the rest
280	  before any port (`uv run tools/gl_budget.py <name>`).
281	- Features TinyGL lacks (`glTexGeni`, `glFog*`, `glInterleavedArrays`) are in
282	  #46, and speeding up the setup cost is #43.
283	
284	Closing, as the survey question is answered and the follow-ups have their own
285	issues.
286	
287	
288	#46 Flying Toasters: what it would take on TinyGL [open]
289	Flying Toasters (`flyingtoasters.c`) is the GL hack Rod would most like. It is
290	a good shape of problem (bounded geometry) but needs three TinyGL extensions
291	and a texture pipeline. Depends on #42 and #43; context in #45.
292	
293	## Geometry is bounded
294	
295	Models in `hacks/glx/toaster*.c` and `toast*.c`, all `GL_N3F_V3F` triangles:
296	
297	| Model | Vertices |
298	| --- | --- |
299	| `toaster` | 366 |
300	| `toaster_base` | 120 |
301	| `toaster_jet` | 168 |
302	| `toaster_slots` | 96 |
303	| `toaster_knob` | 66 |
304	| `toaster_handle` and `toaster_handle2` | 54 and 30 |
305	| `toaster_wing` (two used) | 33 each |
306	| `toast` and `toast2` | 180 and 204 |
307	
308	A toaster is roughly 800 vertices, a slice of toast about 190. The default is
309	20 floaters (`-ntoasters 20`), half toasters, so about 10,000 lit vertices
310	per frame, constant. At about 6 us per vertex plus 80 ms fixed that is about
311	5 fps; `-ntoasters 8` should be near 9. Textures will cost more.
312	
313	## What is missing
314	
315	- Textures: `chromesphere_png.h` and `toast_png.h` (PNG data). There is no PNG
316	  decoder; convert at build time to the raw blob format the logos use
317	  (`tools/make_logo_blob.py`), with the hack's `images/gen/*_png.h` includes
318	  satisfied by generated headers of the same name. TinyGL has one texture
319	  size and format fixed at compile time (`zfeatures.h`), nearest sampling,
320	  no mipmaps, wrapped coordinates.
321	- `glTexGeni` with `GL_SPHERE_MAP`, for the chrome reflection. The enum exists
322	  in TinyGL's header but there is no function. Needs a per-vertex reflection
323	  vector in the vertex path.
324	- Fog: `glFogi(GL_FOG_MODE, GL_EXP2)`, density 0.0085. `glFog*` are declared
325	  but not implemented. Either implement per-vertex fog (blend the lit colour
326	  towards the fog colour) or drop it and lose the distance fade.
327	- `glInterleavedArrays`, which `gllist.c` uses to draw every model. Small:
328	  the array shim from #42 can take it (`GL_N3F_V3F` only).
329	
330	## Plan sketch
331	
332	1. Land the GL layer (#42).
333	2. Add `glInterleavedArrays` to the shim.
334	3. Texture path: build-time PNG to raw, TinyGL texture size, a test with a
335	   known image.
336	4. Sphere-map texgen in TinyGL (patch), with a test.
337	5. Fog, or a decision to omit it.
338	6. Measure, then trim the count with an override if needed.
339	
340

Rod chose Pipes as the first GL hack, TinyGL (C-Chads fork, commit 36a7987) as the rasteriser, "Pipes first, grow later" for scope, and a device speed spike before any spec (2026-10-09). Brainstorming path: architectural, so spec then plan; the spike is the de-risking step.

Facts learned:

- TinyGL's licence is zlib-style, not MIT, and clause 1 requires an acknowledgment in the product and its documentation. Needs a `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` row and README credit if kept.
- Pipes (6.16) does NOT accumulate: every frame it `glClear`s and redraws every piece so far (up to about 500 per system, 5 systems, default) from display lists under a slowly rotating camera. Cost scales with piece count and every frame is a full-frame change. I first told Rod the opposite; that was wrong.
- Pipes needs `sphere.c`, `buildlwo.c`, `teapot.c`, `gltrackball.c`, `rotator.c`, `xlock-gl-utils.c` from `hacks/glx/` (byte-identical copies are allowed there; only `utils/` is off limits).
- Canvas pixels are byte-swapped RGB565 and rows need `canvas_mark_dirty`; the spike swaps and marks on copy.
- Spike code is committed (fe66810) and pushed to `origin/worktree-spike-tinygl`, no PR. It is `firmware/src/hacks/tglspike.c` (top level, because `check_notices.py` treats files in `hacks/<subdir>/` as third-party), envs `spike` and `spike_dump`, guarded by `-DTGL_SPIKE`. The TinyGL copy (`firmware/spike_tinygl/`) is untracked; `firmware/spike_tinygl.patch` rebuilds it from upstream 36a7987 and `docs/tinygl-spike.md` has the steps. Throwaway.
- GL hack survey (146 GL hacks; 87 use textures, 84 blending, 17 fog; only 36 clean of textures/blend/fog/stencil/readback). TinyGL lacks `glTexGeni`, `glFog*` and `glInterleavedArrays`. Flying Toasters needs all three plus two PNG textures (about 10k lit vertices per frame at the default 20 floaters: bounded, unlike Pipes). Candidate first GL hacks are estimates, not measured: gears, morph3d, stonerview, kallisti.
- Upstream TinyGL quirks fixed in the private copy: `memory.c` tests `TGL_FEATURE_CUSTOM_MALLOC` before including its header; `memset_s` clashes with macOS `string.h`.

Device results (2026-10-09, 464x464 16-bit, z-buffer and framebuffer in PSRAM, S3):

- TinyGL display lists cost a 16 KB op buffer each (`OP_BUFFER_MAX_SIZE` 4096); 502 lists overflowed PSRAM and boot-looped (StoreProhibited at 0x4000 in `alloc_list`). Shrinking it to 64 fixed it with an identical picture.
- Stock TinyGL does software double maths in lighting, normalising, matrices (`__muldf3`, `sqrt`, `pow`, `cos`). Single-precision rewrite (`tools/float_literals.py` plus sqrt/pow/sin/cos/floor to the f versions) took a piece from about 13 to 9 ms. Still about 18 us per triangle.
- Bench: full clear 24.8 ms, full-frame copy with byte swap 22.2 ms, 512-triangle sphere 9.2 ms, 32-triangle cylinder 0.59 ms, big 95k-pixel sphere 37.9 ms. Frame at N pieces is roughly N x 8 ms plus about 47 ms fixed, plus the 32 ms push: far too slow for 500 pieces (Pipes redraws everything each frame).
- CORRECTION: the first probe used independent triangles; real Pipes uses triangle strips (unit_sphere 16x16 = 544 vertices) and 24-facet quad-strip tubes, so each vertex is lit once. With faithful primitives: sphere 3.7 ms, tube 0.43 ms, about 3.7 ms per piece (2.8 fps at 80 pieces, 1.2 fps at 210). Real Pipes builds spheres via glVertexPointer/glDrawArrays, which TinyGL display lists may record differently (untested risk).
- Wireframe (`*wireframe: True`: no lighting, 5-facet line-strip tubes, line-strip spheres with 4 vertices per slice) is NOT faster: same frame time as solid. Per-vertex overhead is about 4 us (about 1000 cycles) before lighting, which adds only about 2.8 us; the wire sphere has twice the vertices.
- Low-poly (8x8 sphere): 2.3 ms per piece with independent triangles; same cost per triangle (18 us).
- Rod reported a white screen with nothing visible while the log showed a correct canvas (black corner, coloured centre, no white pixels). Cause unknown at time of writing.

Gears works on the device (2026-10-09/10, commit 2115083 on `worktree-spike-tinygl`, committed locally, NOT yet pushed; Rod loved it):

- Unmodified `gears.c` plus helpers (`involute`, `tube`, `normals`, `rotator`, `gltrackball`, `trackball`, `quaternion`) built by wrappers `firmware/src/hacks/gears_gl.c` and `gl_helper_*.c` (include straight from `vendor/`, `USE_GL` per file, never `HAVE_GL` because it changes `ModeInfo` layout). GL layer in `firmware/src/glshim/` (zero-copy into the canvas with `TGL_SWAP_PIXELS`).
- TinyGL incompatibilities found: display list name 0 is handed out first (hacks abort on `!glGenLists(1)`; fixed by starting at 1); vertex arrays count stride in floats and are read at list replay (shim reroutes the six array calls and expands `glDrawArrays` immediately); `glTexGeni`, `glFog*`, `glInterleavedArrays` missing; `memory.c`, `specbuf_get_buffer` prototype and `memset_s` upstream bugs.
- Speed: heavy fixed-seed scene (17.7k vertices per frame) 4 to 5 fps, light scenes about 9 fps. Per frame: clear 24.6 ms, fill about 40 ms, vertex/triangle setup about 100 to 120 ms (about 6 us per vertex), push 32 ms. `-O2` for TinyGL and specular lookup tables each changed nothing; global `-O2` ICEs on `braid_single.c`. Unexplored levers: triangle setup maths (software float divides), a second core, preferring lighter Gears layouts via overrides.
- Host dump raw files are already un-swapped (`dump_main.c`); `rgb565_to_png.py` reads them as plain RGB565. A script that swaps again shows psychedelic stripes.
- Harness: in a worktree session, commands must be plain (no heredocs, `$VAR`, or complex constructs); `Edit` must use the worktree path, not the shared checkout path.

Landing Gears (Rod approved, 2026-10-10): tracking issue #42, branch `feature/42-gears-gl` (worktree `.claude/worktrees/gears-gl`, based on origin/main 1fa1177). Spike branch `worktree-spike-tinygl` is pushed (2115083). Follow-up issues: #43 TinyGL speed, #44 Pipes, #45 next GL hacks, #46 Flying Toasters, #41 xlockmore docs. Spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-09-gears-gl-design.md` committed (8571f29) on the feature branch and awaiting Rod's review; next step is writing-plans, then TDD. Planning artifacts are not to be merged to main. Rod's decisions: pristine TinyGL copy plus build-time patch; land Gears with its random layouts; Rod granted reflash permission for the Gears work.

Shell gotcha: never `cd` into `vendor/` (a symlink to the main checkout) in a worktree session; the shell gets stuck outside the worktree and `ExitWorktree keep` plus `EnterWorktree path=` is needed to recover.

Related: [[project-xlockmore-docs-stale]].

48	
49	Facts learned:
50	
51	- TinyGL's licence is zlib-style, not MIT, and clause 1 requires an acknowledgment in the product and its documentation. Needs a `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` row and README credit if kept.
52	- Pipes (6.16) does NOT accumulate: every frame it `glClear`s and redraws every piece so far (up to about 500 per system, 5 systems, default) from display lists under a slowly rotating camera. Cost scales with piece count and every frame is a full-frame change. I first told Rod the opposite; that was wrong.
53	- Pipes needs `sphere.c`, `buildlwo.c`, `teapot.c`, `gltrackball.c`, `rotator.c`, `xlock-gl-utils.c` from `hacks/glx/` (byte-identical copies are allowed there; only `utils/` is off limits).
54	- Canvas pixels are byte-swapped RGB565 and rows need `canvas_mark_dirty`; the spike swaps and marks on copy.
55	- Spike code is committed (fe66810) and pushed to `origin/worktree-spike-tinygl`, no PR. It is `firmware/src/hacks/tglspike.c` (top level, because `check_notices.py` treats files in `hacks/<subdir>/` as third-party), envs `spike` and `spike_dump`, guarded by `-DTGL_SPIKE`. The TinyGL copy (`firmware/spike_tinygl/`) is untracked; `firmware/spike_tinygl.patch` rebuilds it from upstream 36a7987 and `docs/tinygl-spike.md` has the steps. Throwaway.
56	- GL hack survey (146 GL hacks; 87 use textures, 84 blending, 17 fog; only 36 clean of textures/blend/fog/stencil/readback). TinyGL lacks `glTexGeni`, `glFog*` and `glInterleavedArrays`. Flying Toasters needs all three plus two PNG textures (about 10k lit vertices per frame at the default 20 floaters: bounded, unlike Pipes). Candidate first GL hacks are estimates, not measured: gears, morph3d, stonerview, kallisti.
57	- Upstream TinyGL quirks fixed in the private copy: `memory.c` tests `TGL_FEATURE_CUSTOM_MALLOC` before including its header; `memset_s` clashes with macOS `string.h`.
58	
59	Device results (2026-10-09, 464x464 16-bit, z-buffer and framebuffer in PSRAM, S3):
60	
61	- TinyGL display lists cost a 16 KB op buffer each (`OP_BUFFER_MAX_SIZE` 4096); 502 lists overflowed PSRAM and boot-looped (StoreProhibited at 0x4000 in `alloc_list`). Shrinking it to 64 fixed it with an identical picture.
62	- Stock TinyGL does software double maths in lighting, normalising, matrices (`__muldf3`, `sqrt`, `pow`, `cos`). Single-precision rewrite (`tools/float_literals.py` plus sqrt/pow/sin/cos/floor to the f versions) took a piece from about 13 to 9 ms. Still about 18 us per triangle.
63	- Bench: full clear 24.8 ms, full-frame copy with byte swap 22.2 ms, 512-triangle sphere 9.2 ms, 32-triangle cylinder 0.59 ms, big 95k-pixel sphere 37.9 ms. Frame at N pieces is roughly N x 8 ms plus about 47 ms fixed, plus the 32 ms push: far too slow for 500 pieces (Pipes redraws everything each frame).
64	- CORRECTION: the first probe used independent triangles; real Pipes uses triangle strips (unit_sphere 16x16 = 544 vertices) and 24-facet quad-strip tubes, so each vertex is lit once. With faithful primitives: sphere 3.7 ms, tube 0.43 ms, about 3.7 ms per piece (2.8 fps at 80 pieces, 1.2 fps at 210). Real Pipes builds spheres via glVertexPointer/glDrawArrays, which TinyGL display lists may record differently (untested risk).
65	- Wireframe (`*wireframe: True`: no lighting, 5-facet line-strip tubes, line-strip spheres with 4 vertices per slice) is NOT faster: same frame time as solid. Per-vertex overhead is about 4 us (about 1000 cycles) before lighting, which adds only about 2.8 us; the wire sphere has twice the vertices.
66	- Low-poly (8x8 sphere): 2.3 ms per piece with independent triangles; same cost per triangle (18 us).
67	- Rod reported a white screen with nothing visible while the log showed a correct canvas (black corner, coloured centre, no white pixels). Cause unknown at time of writing.

69	Gears works on the device (2026-10-09/10, commit 2115083 on `worktree-spike-tinygl`, committed locally, NOT yet pushed; Rod loved it):
70	
71	- Unmodified `gears.c` plus helpers (`involute`, `tube`, `normals`, `rotator`, `gltrackball`, `trackball`, `quaternion`) built by wrappers `firmware/src/hacks/gears_gl.c` and `gl_helper_*.c` (include straight from `vendor/`, `USE_GL` per file, never `HAVE_GL` because it changes `ModeInfo` layout). 72	- TinyGL incompatibilities found: display list name 0 is handed out first (hacks abort on `!glGenLists(1)`; fixed by starting at 1); vertex arrays count stride in floats and are read at list replay (shim reroutes the six array calls and expands `glDrawArrays` immediately); `glTexGeni`, `glFog*`, `glInterleavedArrays` missing; `memory.c`, `specbuf_get_buffer` prototype and `memset_s` upstream bugs.

# GL layer and TinyGL gotchas

OpenGL hacks run on TinyGL, a software OpenGL (C-Chads fork, commit
`36a7987`, zlib-style licence). Issues #42 to #46 hold the numbers and ideas.

- `src/tinygl/` is byte-identical to upstream and excluded from every env.
  `firmware/patch_tinygl.py` runs `tools/tinygl_patch.py` and writes the
  patched tree, plus one unity file, into `.pio/build/<env>/generated/`;
  `glshim/tinygl_build.c` compiles it. Each patch checks its anchor and fails
  with "has upstream changed?". TinyGL's README allows building it as one
  unit, and it compiles cleanly that way.
- A GL hack gets `USE_GL` from a one-line wrapper: `hacks/<name>_gl.c` for
  the hack, `glshim/glx_<name>.c` for each helper copied to
  `xs_support/glx/`. Exclude the copies in all three envs' `build_src_filter`
  and keep `-Isrc/xs_support/glx` in `build_flags`. Never define `HAVE_GL`:
  it adds `glx_context` to `ModeInfo`, which `xlockmore.c` (built without
  it) allocates smaller. Build each helper as its own unit: `tube.h` and
  `normals.h` define clashing types.
- TinyGL draws straight into `canvas->px` at the canvas size, with its
  pixel packer patched to the canvas's byte-swapped RGB565. Test colours
  with exact `rgb565()` values: white looks the same either way round.
- Display list name 0 means "invalid" to hacks (`if (!glGenLists(1)) abort()`)
  and TinyGL handed it out first; the patch starts at 1. Its list buffers
  are 64 slots, not 4,096: each list took 16 KB and 500 lists overflowed
  PSRAM (boot loop, `StoreProhibited` at `0x4000` in `alloc_list`).
- TinyGL counts vertex-array stride in floats and reads the array when a
  display list is replayed; GL counts bytes and reads at the draw call, and
  hacks free the array straight after (`tube.c`, `sphere.c`). Hacks'
  `glVertexPointer` and friends are renamed to `glshim_*` by macros in
  `glshim.h`, and `glDrawArrays` expands at once. The symptom of the old
  behaviour was needles through the tubes.

  `xshim_set_release_hook`, which `xshim_release_pixmaps` (the runner's
  `stop()`) runs. A second `init_GL` replaces the first, which hides a
  missing hook, so test `glshim_is_open()` right after the hack stops.

  allocation only. `glInit`'s own allocations (lists, matrix stacks) are
  unchecked upstream, so running out of PSRAM after the z-buffer crashes there.
- `glDrawArrays` reads every client array as `GL_FLOAT` and ignores the type
  argument: check a new hack's `glVertexPointer` calls before trusting it.

  application calls `glSetEnableSpecular(1)`, so Gears has no highlights
  and `glMateriali` is invisible without it. Enabling it costs speed (#43).
- TinyGL lacks `glTexGeni`, `glFog*` and `glInterleavedArrays` (#46). The
  header declares `glFog*` and the `GL_SPHERE_MAP` enum; the library defines
  neither.

  so a line that moves a little jumps a whole pixel somewhere along its length:

  keeps the fractional position (`zp.fx`, `zp.fy`) and draws a line with Wu's
  algorithm when a hack enables `GL_LINE_SMOOTH`. Only lines get it; filled
  triangles are still snapped. A line whose two colours differ is drawn plain.

  Unknown Pleasures' per-row fade (`glColor4f` with an eased alpha) does not
  happen and every ridge draws at full intensity. Rod approved that look on the
  device and closed the review finding as wontfix.

  function's alpha, and decodes pixels as if they were not byte-swapped, so
  it is only right for black and white. A white-on-black frame hides this, and
  smooth (grey) lines did not. The fill wrapper (`gl_draw_triangle_fill` in
  `tinygl_patch.py`) treats `SRC_ALPHA, ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA`, which is alpha 1
  in real GL, as an opaque fill. Other blend functions still use the macro and
  are wrong for any colour but black and white.

  direction, and with only the hack's offset each quad still ate a few percent

  `|dz/dx| + |dz/dy|` whenever an offset is asked for (not for an offset of 0, 0).

  offset, about 500 (the floor) with the margin. An earlier depth-fighting
  experiment found no effect only because blending made every quad invisible:
  change one thing at a time, and check that the thing under test can act.

  pulls toward the viewer, so a positive margin would weaken it), the bias is
  clamped to about +/-2^29, and each shifted vertex depth is clamped to the
  16-bit range with the originals restored exactly: an offset that carried a

  a second fill slightly behind the first, because a twin at equal depth wins
  a tie either way and cannot tell the signs apart.

  defensive otherwise; `test_glshim` uses `glViewport(0, 0, 2 * SIZE, 2 * SIZE)`

  push 32 ms): Gears runs at 4 to 5 fps for its heaviest layout and about 9
  for light ones. `-O2` for TinyGL and specular lookup tables changed

  2.5 MB. Measure leaks while stopped, not by comparing two running moments.

  AddressSanitizer) is not the board's (2.4 KB used in the spike); the host
  test is a tripwire and the board is the proof.

  them as plain RGB565. Swapping them again gives psychedelic stripes.

  instrumented copy of TinyGL (`instrument()` adds the counters after

  over-predicts few-large-triangle scenes, and lines and points cost nothing
  beyond vertex setup. Add a second calibration point after each GL port.

  the object to 0.3 and moves it on a Lissajous path, so it is about 70 px
  across on the 466 px canvas and its position differs frame to frame. It
  cannot be enlarged without patching the hack. It enables two lights and

  on a 64-bit host (fine on the 32-bit board); it has a patch-level test only.

# GL budget: cubicgrid and morph3d

`tools/gl_budget.py` runs a GL hack on the host, counts what each frame asks of
TinyGL, and predicts the device frame time. It was built to choose between two
candidates for the next GL port (issue #45) without flashing either.

```text
uv run tools/gl_budget.py [--frames N] [--seeds a,b,c]
    [--override '*name: value' ...] name[:seed] ...
```

Gears is read from `firmware/src/hacks/gears/`; any other name from
`vendor/xscreensaver-6.16/hacks/glx/` (git-ignored, never copied into the
repo). A hack that does not build is reported with its first error, and the
exit status is 1.

`--override` gives the hack a resource line that beats its own defaults, as an
entry in `registry.c`'s override list does on the device. Repeat it for more.
It applies to every hack named, so run hacks with different overrides
separately. Use it to try a registry override (`--override '*count: 40'`)
before committing to it, or to supply one a hack needs to start.

## What it counts

The counters sit inside a private copy of TinyGL, built only for the tool
(`firmware/src/tinygl/` and the firmware builds are untouched). Counting there
means a display list that is built once and replayed every frame is counted on
every frame. Per frame, it records:

- **Vertices** set up, and how many of them were lit.
- **Triangles** rasterised, after back-face culling, and the **pixels** they
  cover (screen area, overdraw included, capped at the canvas).
- **Lines** and **points** drawn.

## The cost model

A frame costs a fixed 56.6 ms (clear 24.6 ms, display push 32 ms), plus 4 us
per vertex, 2.8 us more for each enabled light on each lit vertex (both from the
Pipes probe in #43, measured with one light), plus a fill term. The fill term
is 570 ns a pixel, fitted so that the heavy Gears scene (seed 13, 17,700
vertices) costs the 40 ms of fill that #43 measured.

Checked against Gears, the only hack with device numbers. The fit and the
tests use 60 frames; the table below is a 300 frame run, and Gears' pixel
count drifts by about 15 percent between the two as the gears turn (at 60
frames the heavy scene is 217 ms and its fill is exactly 40 ms; at 300 it is
211 ms and 34 ms):

| Scene | Predicted | Measured (#43) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Gears seed 13, heavy | 211 ms, 4.7 fps | 197 to 217 ms, about 5 fps |
| Gears seed 11, light (held out) | 117 ms, 8.5 fps | about 111 ms, 9 fps |

The light scene was not used in the fit and lands within 6 percent.

## The comparison

Means over 300 frames after a 10 frame warm-up. Both hacks are lit or point
based, so the fixed 56.6 ms sets a ceiling of about 17.7 fps for anything.

| Hack | Vertices | Triangles | Points | Predicted | fps |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| morph3d, four of its five shapes (seeds 1 to 8) | 3,864 to 7,200 | 2,300 to 4,000 | 0 | 87 to 114 ms | 8.8 to 11.5 |
| cubicgrid, default `ticks` 30 | 27,000 | 0 | 27,000 | 165 ms | 6.1 |

  light, while the model's lighting cost was measured with one (about +20 ms

- **cubicgrid** draws a 30 by 30 by 30 grid of points (`ticks` cubed) from a

  why it lands at about 6 fps. The model does not cost the points themselves,

188	separately. Use it to try a registry override (`--override '*count: 40'`)
189	before committing to it, or to supply one a hack needs to start.
190	
191	## What it counts
192	
193	The counters sit inside a private copy of TinyGL, built only for the tool
194	(`firmware/src/tinygl/` and the firmware builds are untouched). Counting there
195	means a display list that is built once and replayed every frame is counted on
196	every frame. Per frame, it records:
197	
198	- **Vertices** set up, and how many of them were lit.
199	- **Triangles** rasterised, after back-face culling, and the **pixels** they
200	  cover (screen area, overdraw included, capped at the canvas).
201	- **Lines** and **points** drawn.
202	
203	## The cost model
204	
205	A frame costs a fixed 56.6 ms (clear 24.6 ms, display push 32 ms), plus 4 us
206	per vertex, 2.8 us more for each enabled light on each lit vertex (both from the
207	Pipes probe in #43, measured with one light), plus a fill term. The fill term
208	is 570 ns a pixel, fitted so that the heavy Gears scene (seed 13, 17,700
209	vertices) costs the 40 ms of fill that #43 measured.
210	
211	Checked against Gears, the only hack with device numbers. The fit and the
212	tests use 60 frames; the table below is a 300 frame run, and Gears' pixel
213	count drifts by about 15 percent between the two as the gears turn (at 60
214	frames the heavy scene is 217 ms and its fill is exactly 40 ms; at 300 it is
215	211 ms and 34 ms):
216	
217	| Scene | Predicted | Measured (#43) |
218	| --- | --- | --- |
219	| Gears seed 13, heavy | 211 ms, 4.7 fps | 197 to 217 ms, about 5 fps |
220	| Gears seed 11, light (held out) | 117 ms, 8.5 fps | about 111 ms, 9 fps |
221	
222	The light scene was not used in the fit and lands within 6 percent.
223	
224	## The comparison
225	
226	Means over 300 frames after a 10 frame warm-up. Both hacks are lit or point
227	based, so the fixed 56.6 ms sets a ceiling of about 17.7 fps for anything.
228	
229	| Hack | Vertices | Triangles | Points | Predicted | fps |
230	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
231	| morph3d, four of its five shapes (seeds 1 to 8) | 3,864 to 7,200 | 2,300 to 4,000 | 0 | 87 to 114 ms | 8.8 to 11.5 |
232	| cubicgrid, default `ticks` 30 | 27,000 | 0 | 27,000 | 165 ms | 6.1 |
233	
234	- **morph3d** is lit and vertex-bound, but treat 9 to 11 fps as optimistic.
235	  It enables two lights and two-sided lighting, and TinyGL shades once per
236	  light, while the model's lighting cost was measured with one (about +20 ms
237	  for seed 1). Its triangles are also tiny, 3 to 4 pixels each against 15 to
238	  29 in the Gears scenes the fill figure was fitted to. The fill term absorbs
239	  per-triangle cost at Gears' ratio, so it under-predicts here: if all of
240	  Gears' fill were per-triangle cost, morph3d's would be about 35 ms rather
241	  than 8. Together these could put morph3d nearer 6 to 8 fps.
242	- **cubicgrid** draws a 30 by 30 by 30 grid of points (`ticks` cubed) from a
243	  display list every frame. At the default that is 27,000 vertices, which is
244	  why it lands at about 6 fps. The model does not cost the points themselves,
245	  and they are drawn 2.5 pixels wide (`bigdots` defaults to True), so 6 fps is
246	  an optimistic floor too.
247	- Its size is a resource. Setting `*ticks` through a `HackEntry` override, as
248	  Galaxy does with `*count`, shrinks the cost with the cube, by the same
249	  arithmetic (vertices only, no point cost): `ticks` 20 gives 8,000 points,
250	  about 89 ms and 11 fps; 15 gives 3,375, about 70 ms and 14 fps.
251	
252	## Verdict
253	
254	Port **morph3d** first, but the margin is narrower than the first numbers
255	suggested. Both hacks are optimistic for reasons the model cannot see, and by
256	different amounts. morph3d needs no override and should land in the high single
257	digits; cubicgrid at its default is at best 6 fps and probably worse, and needs
258	a `*ticks` override of about 15 to 20 to be competitive. morph3d is also a lit,
259	morphing solid, which is what the GL layer is for. Port **cubicgrid** second,
260	once morph3d has given us a second point to check the model against, and the
261	tool can be taught the two-light and small-triangle cases from it.
262	
263	The numbers say what each frame costs, not how it looks: a dot lattice at 14
264	fps and a morphing polyhedron at 10 fps are different bets on what Rod will
265	want to see on the board.
266	
267	## Accuracy against the device
268	
269	Gears, Morph3D, CubicGrid and Unknown Pleasures have all now run on the
270	board. The predictions below were committed before each port was flashed
271	(Unknown Pleasures' in its commit message). Measured is step plus push, the
272	quantity the model predicts, with the wait for the panel's TE pulse left out.
273	Error is measured against predicted.
274	
275	| Scene | Predicted | Measured | Error |
276	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
277	| Gears heavy, seed 13 | 211 ms | about 207 ms (#43) | in-sample, fitted |
278	| Gears light, seed 11 | 117 ms | about 111 ms (#43) | +5% (held out) |
279	| Morph3D, 5,040 or 5,100 vertices (corrected, see below) | 98 to 100 ms | 111 to 118 ms | +11% to +20% |
280	| Morph3D, 2,300 vertices (not in the first survey) | none | 84 ms | |
281	| CubicGrid, 27,000 points | 165 ms | 170 to 180 ms | +3% to +9% |
282	| CubicGrid, 8,000 points | 89 ms | 80 to 88 ms | -10% to -1% |
283	| Unknown Pleasures, 40 rows of 100 points, as first flashed | 251 ms | 267 ms | +6% |
284	| Unknown Pleasures, 20 rows of 50 points, as first flashed | 197 ms | 186 ms | -6% |
285	| Unknown Pleasures, 40 rows, after the fixes | 251 ms (same counts) | 197 ms | -22% |
286	| Unknown Pleasures, 20 rows, after the fixes, on a later main | 197 ms (same counts) | about 124 ms | -37% |
287	
288	- **Good to about 10 percent for Gears and CubicGrid; Morph3D was 11 to 20
289	  percent too optimistic** (see the correction below), until the model charged
290	  each enabled light. It ranked them correctly throughout, which is the use it
291	  was built for: choosing which hack to port and what to turn down.
292	- **The Gears rows are weaker evidence than the rest.** Their "measured"
293	  figures are the breakdown quoted in issue #43, not a capture made for this
294	  comparison, and the fill figure was fitted to the heavy one.
295	- **Correction (from the overnight capture, below).** An earlier version of
296	  this table matched Morph3D's measured steps to its shapes by size alone and
297	  called them the 7,200 and 3,864 vertex shapes, giving errors of -3 percent to

300	  under-predicted by 11 to 20 percent. The device does not seed `random()`, so a
301	  start cannot be asked for its shape; shapes are matched by the order of their
302	  step times, which must follow vertex count.
303	- **The review's worry about lights was right.** Morph3D has two lights and the
304	  model charged one lit cost per vertex. Charging 2.8 us for each enabled light

307	  45, 65, 81 and 102 inferred. Its tiny triangles and CubicGrid's wide points

"""PlatformIO pre-build script: writes the patched TinyGL tree, and the one
translation unit that includes it, into the build directory. The tree in
src/tinygl/ stays byte-identical to upstream; see tools/tinygl_patch.py."""

import sys
from pathlib import Path

Import("env")  # noqa: F821

project = Path(env["PROJECT_DIR"])  # noqa: F821
sys.path.insert(0, str(project.parent / "tools"))
import tinygl_patch  # noqa: E402

source = project / "src" / "tinygl"
sources = {
    str(path.relative_to(source)): path.read_text(errors="surrogateescape")
    for sub in ("src", "include")
    for path in sorted((source / sub).rglob("*"))
    if path.is_file()
}
patched = tinygl_patch.patch_tree(sources)

generated = Path(env.subst("$BUILD_DIR")) / "generated"  # noqa: F821


def write_if_changed(path: Path, text: str) -> None:
    """Rewrites only a changed file, so the build does not recompile it."""
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    data = text.encode(errors="surrogateescape")
    if not path.exists() or path.read_bytes() != data:
        path.write_bytes(data)


for relative, text in patched.items():
    write_if_changed(generated / "tinygl" / relative, text)
write_if_changed(generated / "tinygl_unity.c", tinygl_patch.unity_source(patched))

# `GL/gl.h` and `zbuffer.h` resolve to the patched copy, and
# src/glshim/tinygl_build.c finds the unity file.
env.Append(  # noqa: F821
    CPPPATH=[str(generated / "tinygl" / "include"), str(generated)]
)

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Predict the device frame rate of GL hacks from host counts."
    )

    parser.add_argument(
        "--override",
        dest="overrides",

        default=[],

        help="a resource line that beats the hack's defaults, as a registry "
        "override does on the device; repeat for more, applies to every hack named",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--seeds",
        default=",".join(map(str, DEFAULT_SEEDS)),

    )
    parser.add_argument(

    )
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    seeds = [int(seed) for seed in args.seeds.split(",")]
    parsed = []
    for spec in args.hacks:
        name, _, seed = spec.partition(":")
        parsed.append((name, [int(seed)] if seed else seeds))
    args.hacks = parsed
    return args


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:

def write_tinygl(root: Path, generated: Path) -> None:
    """The instrumented TinyGL tree and its unity file, where the firmware's
    build puts the patched one."""
    tree = load_tinygl(root)
    for relative, text in tree.items():
        path = generated / "tinygl" / relative
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        path.write_bytes(text.encode(errors="surrogateescape"))
    (generated / "tinygl_unity.c").write_text(tinygl_patch.unity_source(tree))

    ("*count: 40") that beat the hack's own defaults."""
    try:

                f"-I{generated}",
                str(tmp / f"{name}.c"),

                *map(str, shim_sources(root)),
                "-lm",
                "-lpthread",
                "-o",
                str(program),
            ]
            build = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, check=False)
            if build.returncode != 0:

"""Patches that make TinyGL run on the StopWatch.

The copy in `firmware/src/tinygl/` stays byte-identical to upstream (the
C-Chads fork, commit 36a7987). The firmware build writes a patched tree into
the build directory with `firmware/patch_tinygl.py` and compiles that, as it
does for Maze and Pacman. Each patch checks what it replaces and fails loudly
if upstream has changed.

What the patches do, and why:

- 16-bit pixels, written byte-swapped: the canvas holds RGB565 with its bytes
  already swapped into display order, so TinyGL draws straight into it with no
  copy.
- A PSRAM-aware allocator: the z-buffer is 434 KB and the internal heap is
  325 KB.
- `glGenLists` starts at 1: hacks treat list name 0 as "invalid" and abort.
- `OP_BUFFER_MAX_SIZE` is 64, not 4096: every display list otherwise takes a
  16 KB buffer, and Pipes alone makes 500 of them.
- The buffer width is not rounded down to a multiple of 4: the canvas is 466.
- `memset_s` is renamed: macOS's `string.h` declares its own.
- A dirty rectangle: TinyGL reports the box around everything it draws to
  `src/glshim/glshim.c`, which clears only the box drawn since the last clear
  and marks only that box (and the one it replaced) for the display push.
- Smooth lines: `glEnable(GL_LINE_SMOOTH)` is honoured. Vertices keep their
  fractional position (`zp.fx`, `zp.fy`), and a line is drawn with Wu's
  algorithm, blended over what is there.
- Filled triangles honour polygon offset, and treat `SRC_ALPHA,
  ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA` as opaque (TinyGL has no alpha).
- Single precision: the S3's FPU does only `float`, so `double` maths is
  software. Decimal literals get an `f` suffix (`float_literals.py`) and
  `sqrt`, `pow`, `sin`, `cos` and `floor` map to their `f` versions.

import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))

import float_literals as fl  # noqa: E402
import tinygl_patch as tp  # noqa: E402

TINYGL = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "firmware" / "src" / "tinygl"


def load_sources() -> dict[str, str]:
    """The committed, byte-identical copy, keyed as the build script keys it."""
    return {
        str(p.relative_to(TINYGL)): p.read_text(errors="surrogateescape")
        for sub in ("src", "include")
        for p in sorted((TINYGL / sub).rglob("*"))
        if p.is_file()
    }


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def patched() -> dict[str, str]:
    return tp.patch_tree(load_sources())


def test_patch_tree_applies_every_listed_change(patched):
    features = patched["include/zfeatures.h"]
    assert "TGL_FEATURE_16_BITS        1" in features
    assert "TGL_FEATURE_32_BITS        0" in features
    assert "TGL_FEATURE_CUSTOM_MALLOC 1" in features
    assert "TGL_SWAP16" in patched["include/zbuffer.h"]
    zbuffer = patched["src/zbuffer.c"]
    assert "xsize & ~3" not in zbuffer
    assert not re.search(r"(?<!tgl_)memset_s", zbuffer)
    assert "for (i = 1; i < MAX_DISPLAY_LISTS; i++)" in patched["src/list.c"]
    assert "#define OP_BUFFER_MAX_SIZE 64" in patched["src/zgl.h"]
    assert '#include "tinygl_single.h"' in patched["src/zgl.h"]
    assert '#include "tinygl_single.h"' in patched["src/zmath.h"]
    memory = patched["src/memory.c"]
    assert "heap_caps_malloc" in memory and "192" in memory
    single = patched["src/tinygl_single.h"]
    for name in ("sqrt", "pow", "sin", "cos", "floor"):
        assert f"#define {name} {name}f" in single


@pytest.mark.parametrize("path", tp.FLOAT_LITERAL_FILES)
def test_float_literals_are_applied_to_the_listed_files(patched, path):
    # float_literals raises when it finds nothing left to suffix.
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="no floating-point literals"):
        fl.float_literals(patched[path])


@pytest.mark.parametrize("path", tp.FLOAT_LITERAL_FILES)
def test_every_listed_file_has_literals_upstream(path):
    fl.float_literals(load_sources()[path])


def anchor_id(rep: "tp.Replace") -> str:
    return f"{rep.path}:{rep.anchor[:24]!r}"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("rep", tp.REPLACEMENTS, ids=anchor_id)
def test_a_missing_anchor_names_upstream_as_the_problem(rep):
    sources = load_sources()
    sources[rep.path] = sources[rep.path].replace(rep.anchor, "")
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="has upstream changed"):
        tp.patch_tree(sources)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("rep", tp.REPLACEMENTS, ids=anchor_id)

    sources = load_sources()
    sources[rep.path] += "\n" + rep.anchor
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="has upstream changed"):
        tp.patch_tree(sources)

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Hot:
    """A function on TinyGL's per-vertex or per-triangle path, found by its
    definition line in the patched tree. It is marked `TGL_HOT` (IRAM when
    built with GL_IRAM). With a `slot` it is also timed under GL_PROFILE:
    the body moves to `<name>_timed` and the old name wraps it in a cycle
    count. `reentrant` times only the outermost call (lists call lists)."""

    path: str
    definition: str
    call: str = ""
    slot: str = ""
    reentrant: bool = False

    @property
    def anchor(self) -> str:
        return self.definition + " {\n"

    def replacement(self) -> str:
        if not self.slot:
            return "TGL_HOT " + self.anchor
        head, params = self.definition.split("(", 1)
        ret, name = head.rsplit(" ", 1)
        timed = f"{ret} {name}_timed({params}"
        if self.reentrant:
            body = (
                "\tstatic int depth;\n"
                f"\tif (depth++) {{\n\t\t{name}_timed({self.call});\n\t\tdepth--;\n\t\treturn;\n\t}}\n"
                "\tconst uint32_t prof_start = glshim_prof_now();\n"
                f"\t{name}_timed({self.call});\n"
                f"\tglshim_prof_add({self.slot}, prof_start);\n"
                "\tdepth--;\n"
            )
        else:
            body = (
                "\tconst uint32_t prof_start = glshim_prof_now();\n"
                f"\t{name}_timed({self.call});\n"
                f"\tglshim_prof_add({self.slot}, prof_start);\n"
            )
        return (
            "#ifdef GL_PROFILE\n"
            f"static {timed};\n"
            f"TGL_HOT {self.anchor}{body}}}\n"
            f"TGL_HOT static {timed} {{\n"
            "#else\n"
            f"TGL_HOT {self.anchor}"
            "#endif\n"
        )

def instrument(sources: Mapping[str, str]) -> dict[str, str]:

def hot_id(hot: "tp.Hot") -> str:
    return f"{hot.path}:{hot.definition.split('(')[0].split()[-1]}"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("hot", tp.HOT_FUNCTIONS, ids=hot_id)
def test_every_hot_function_is_marked_and_timed_if_it_has_a_slot(patched, hot):
    """GL_IRAM moves exactly these functions; GL_PROFILE times the ones with
    a slot from their first line."""
    text = patched[hot.path]
    assert text.count("TGL_HOT " + hot.anchor) == 1
    if hot.slot:
        scope = "GLPROF_SCOPE_OUTER" if hot.reentrant else "GLPROF_SCOPE"
        assert f"TGL_HOT {hot.anchor}\t{scope}({hot.slot});\n" in text


@pytest.mark.parametrize("hot", tp.HOT_FUNCTIONS, ids=hot_id)
def test_a_missing_hot_function_names_upstream_as_the_problem(hot):
    sources = load_sources()
    patched_once = tp.patch_tree(sources)
    assert hot.anchor not in patched_once[hot.path].replace("TGL_HOT " + hot.anchor, "")
    broken = dict(sources)
    upstream_anchor = hot.anchor if hot.anchor in sources[hot.path] else None
    if upstream_anchor is None:  # written by an earlier patch: break that one
        pytest.skip("anchor is written by FILL_TRIANGLE")
    broken[hot.path] = sources[hot.path].replace(hot.anchor, hot.anchor.replace("(", " ("))
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="has upstream changed"):
        tp.patch_tree(broken)


def test_only_the_list_call_is_timed_as_reentrant():
    """Display lists call lists; timing every level would count time twice."""
    assert [h.definition for h in tp.HOT_FUNCTIONS if h.reentrant] == [
        "void glopCallList(GLParam* p)"
    ]

"""Reads the StopWatch's serial log into a file for a number of seconds.

    .venv/bin/python -I tools/serial_capture.py <out-file> <seconds> [port]

Opening the port resets the board (a random hack starts, the overlay returns to
nothing), and a flash or a crash makes the port go away and come back, so this
reopens it in a loop. Run it in the background with absolute paths; background
shells ignore `cd`. The `run <hack> fps= step= push= ...` lines are explained in
AGENTS.md ("Serial log").
"""

import sys
import time

import serial

DEFAULT_PORT = "/dev/cu.usbmodem112401"


def capture(out: str, seconds: float, port: str = DEFAULT_PORT) -> None:
    end = time.time() + seconds
    with open(out, "wb") as f:
        while time.time() < end:
            try:
                with serial.Serial(port, 115200, timeout=1) as s:
                    while time.time() < end:
                        f.write(s.read(4096))
                        f.flush()
            except (serial.SerialException, OSError):
                time.sleep(0.5)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) not in (3, 4):
        sys.exit(__doc__)
    capture(sys.argv[1], float(sys.argv[2]), *(sys.argv[3:]))

"""Flash builds of the firmware in turn and compare their serial logs.

    .venv/bin/python -I tools/ab_flash.py --hack CubicGrid --seconds 60 \\
        --rounds 2 --out /tmp/ab base= iram=-DGL_IRAM "prof=-DGL_PROFILE -DGL_IRAM"

Each `name=flags` is a variant. Every variant is built once, pinned to the
hack with rotation off (`START_HACK`, `ROTATE_SECONDS=0`), and its image kept.
Then, round by round, each image is flashed and the serial log captured for
`--seconds`. A boot is deterministic, so alternating builds and comparing
window by window is how this repo measures a change (AGENTS.md).

This flashes the device: run it only with Rod's go-ahead. It never touches
the partition table or `ffat`; `pio run -t upload` writes what a normal
upload writes.
"""

import argparse
import os
import re
import shutil
import statistics
import subprocess
import sys
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
FIRMWARE = ROOT / "firmware"
IMAGE = FIRMWARE / ".pio" / "build" / "stopwatch" / "firmware.bin"

RUN = re.compile(r"^run (?P<hack>\S+) (?P<fields>.*)$")
GLPROF = re.compile(r"^glprof (?P<hack>\S+) (?P<fields>.*)$")
FIELD = re.compile(r"(\w+)=([-\d.]+)")


def parse_fields(text: str) -> dict[str, float]:
    """`fps=12.3 step=45.6ms rows=466` to {"fps": 12.3, "step": 45.6, ...}."""
    return {k: float(v) for k, v in FIELD.findall(text)}


@dataclass
class Capture:
    runs: list[dict[str, float]] = field(default_factory=list)
    glprof: list[dict[str, float]] = field(default_factory=list)


def parse_log(text: str, hack: str) -> Capture:
    """The `run` and `glprof` windows a log has for `hack` (any case)."""
    out = Capture()
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        line = raw.strip()
        for pattern, bucket in ((RUN, out.runs), (GLPROF, out.glprof)):
            m = pattern.match(line)
            if m and m.group("hack").lower() == hack.lower():
                bucket.append(parse_fields(m.group("fields")))
    return out


def summarise(windows: list[dict[str, float]], skip: int = 1) -> dict[str, float]:
    """Mean of each field, leaving out the first `skip` windows: the first
    holds the boot and, for push, the name overlay (AGENTS.md)."""
    kept = windows[skip:]
    if not kept:
        return {}
    keys = sorted({k for w in kept for k in w})
    return {k: statistics.fmean(w[k] for w in kept if k in w) for k in keys}


def render(results: dict[str, list[Capture]], keys: list[str]) -> str:
    lines = [
        "| Variant | Round | Windows | " + " | ".join(keys) + " |",
        "| --- | --- | --- | " + " | ".join("---" for _ in keys) + " |",
    ]
    for name, captures in results.items():
        for i, cap in enumerate(captures, 1):
            merged = summarise(cap.runs)
            merged.update(summarise(cap.glprof))
            cells = [f"{merged[k]:.2f}" if k in merged else "-" for k in keys]
            lines.append(f"| {name} | {i} | {max(len(cap.runs) - 1, 0)} | " + " | ".join(cells) + " |")
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def pio(*args: str, flags: str = "") -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    env = {
        **os.environ,
        "PLATFORMIO_CORE_DIR": str(ROOT / ".platformio"),
        "NO_COLOR": "1",
        "PLATFORMIO_BUILD_FLAGS": flags,
    }
    return subprocess.run(
        [str(ROOT / ".venv" / "bin" / "pio"), "run", "-d", str(FIRMWARE), "-e", "stopwatch", *args],
        env=env,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=False,
    )


def build(name: str, flags: str, hack: str, out: Path) -> Path:
    pinned = f'-DSTART_HACK=\\"{hack}\\" -DROTATE_SECONDS=0 {flags}'.strip()
    result = pio(flags=pinned)
    (out / f"build-{name}.log").write_text(result.stdout + result.stderr)
    if result.returncode != 0:
        sys.exit(f"build of {name} failed; see {out / f'build-{name}.log'}")
    image = out / f"{name}.bin"
    shutil.copyfile(IMAGE, image)
    return image


def flash(image: Path, log: Path) -> None:
    shutil.copyfile(image, IMAGE)
    result = pio("-t", "nobuild", "-t", "upload")
    log.write_text(result.stdout + result.stderr)
    if result.returncode != 0 or "Hash of data verified" not in result.stdout:
        sys.exit(f"flash of {image.name} did not verify; see {log}")


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    parser.add_argument("--hack", required=True, help="a name from g_hacks[]")
    parser.add_argument("--seconds", type=float, default=60)
    parser.add_argument("--rounds", type=int, default=2)
    parser.add_argument("--out", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--keys", default="fps,step,push,rows")
    parser.add_argument("variants", nargs="+", help="name=flags")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "tools"))
    import serial_capture

    args.out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    variants = dict(v.split("=", 1) for v in args.variants)
    images = {name: build(name, flags, args.hack, args.out) for name, flags in variants.items()}
    results: dict[str, list[Capture]] = {name: [] for name in variants}
    for r in range(1, args.rounds + 1):
        for name, image in images.items():
            flash(image, args.out / f"flash-{r}-{name}.log")
            log = args.out / f"serial-{r}-{name}.log"
            serial_capture.capture(str(log), args.seconds)
            results[name].append(parse_log(log.read_text(errors="replace"), args.hack))
    table = render(results, args.keys.split(","))
    (args.out / "summary.md").write_text(table)
    print(table, end="")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))

import ab_flash  # noqa: E402

LOG = """\
ESP-ROM:esp32s3-20210327
rotate -> CubicGrid heap=300000 psram=7000000
run CubicGrid fps=11.0 step=50.0ms push=40.0ms sync=0.0ms wait=0.0ms rows=466 heap=1 psram=2
glprof CubicGrid frames=55 clear=9.00ms list=30.00ms nvertex=8000
run CubicGrid fps=12.0 step=46.0ms push=33.0ms sync=0.0ms wait=0.0ms rows=466 heap=1 psram=2
glprof CubicGrid frames=60 clear=8.00ms list=28.00ms nvertex=8000
run Gears fps=99.0 step=1.0ms push=1.0ms sync=0.0ms wait=0.0ms rows=1 heap=1 psram=2
run CubicGrid fps=13.0 step=44.0ms push=31.0ms sync=0.0ms wait=0.0ms rows=465 heap=1 psram=2
"""


def test_a_log_gives_the_hacks_windows_in_order():
    cap = ab_flash.parse_log(LOG, "cubicgrid")
    assert [w["step"] for w in cap.runs] == [50.0, 46.0, 44.0]
    assert [w["list"] for w in cap.glprof] == [30.0, 28.0]
    assert cap.runs[0]["rows"] == 466


def test_the_first_window_is_left_out_of_the_mean():
    cap = ab_flash.parse_log(LOG, "CubicGrid")
    mean = ab_flash.summarise(cap.runs)
    assert mean["step"] == 45.0
    assert mean["push"] == 32.0
    assert ab_flash.summarise(cap.runs[:1]) == {}


def test_the_table_has_a_row_per_variant_and_round():
    cap = ab_flash.parse_log(LOG, "CubicGrid")
    table = ab_flash.render({"base": [cap, cap], "iram": [cap]}, ["step", "list", "missing"])
    rows = table.splitlines()
    assert rows[0] == "| Variant | Round | Windows | step | list | missing |"
    assert len(rows) == 5
    assert rows[2] == "| base | 1 | 2 | 45.00 | 28.00 | - |"

def late_id(rep: "tp.Replace") -> str:
    return f"{rep.path}:{rep.anchor[:28]!r}"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("rep", tp.LATE_REPLACEMENTS, ids=late_id)
def test_a_late_anchor_that_moved_is_refused(rep, monkeypatch):
    """Late anchors are written by earlier patches, so break them there."""
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        tp,
        "LATE_REPLACEMENTS",
        tuple(
            tp.Replace(r.path, r.anchor + "\x00", r.replacement, r.count) if r is rep else r
            for r in tp.LATE_REPLACEMENTS
        ),
    )
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="has upstream changed"):
        tp.patch_tree(load_sources())


def test_lazy_lighting_shades_before_every_draw(patched):
    """Every place a lit vertex reaches the rasteriser shades it first."""
    clip = patched["src/clip.c"]
    assert clip.count("GL_SHADE_NOW3(p0, p1, p2); glshim_note_triangle") == 4
    assert "GL_SHADE_NOW3(p0, p1, p2);\n\t\t\tgl_draw_triangle_clip(p0, p1, p2, 0);" in clip
    assert "GL_SHADE_NOW(p0);" in clip
    assert "GL_SHADE_NOW(p1);\n\tGL_SHADE_NOW(p2);" in clip


def test_clip_temporaries_are_never_shaded_again(patched):
    """The clipper's stack vertices are interpolated from shaded ones and go
    back through gl_draw_triangle; an uninitialised flag shaded them with the
    material (a host test caught it as half-bright fills, depending on what
    the stack held)."""
    clip = patched["src/clip.c"]
    tmp = clip[clip.index("static void updateTmp") :]
    assert "q->shade_pending = 0;" in tmp[: tmp.index("q->color.v[0]")]


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "op",
    [
        "glopMaterial",
        "glopLight",
        "glopLightModel",
        "glopSetEnableSpecular",
        "glopEnableDisable",
    ],
)
def test_lighting_state_changes_shade_what_is_pending_first(patched, op):
    text = patched["src/misc.c" if op == "glopEnableDisable" else "src/light.c"]
    body = text[text.index(f"void {op}(GLParam* p) {{") :]
    assert "GL_SHADE_FLUSH();" in body[:120]
EOF

# Porting an xscreensaver hack

The rules live in `AGENTS.md` ("Rules", "Gotchas") and the path-scoped notes in
`.claude/rules/`. This skill sets the order of work and the points to stop. The
numbered steps are in `adding-a-hack.md` and the recipes it names are in
`techniques.md`, both next to this file. For several hacks in one go, read
`batches.md` too.

## 1. Pick, then read the source

Take S-rated rows from `docs/porting-assessment.md` first, and prefer a low
**Speed** band: the table runs each unported S hack on the host. The effort
rating counts missing shim calls, not memory, speed or stack (Braid was S, and
would have shown as high). A high band is a hack that will probably run slowly
on the board; a low band is not a guarantee, because a hack still doing
software `double` maths runs far slower on the device than on the host. Read
the hack's source before copying it, and look for:

| The source has | Technique (seen in) |
| --- | --- |
| Arrays or a state over a few MB | Build-time patch (Maze) |
| `sin`, `cos`, `sqrt`, `pow`, `double` in a hot loop | Single precision (Galaxy, Substrate) |
| Locals over a few KB | Stack check (Rorschach) |
| An allocation of 100 KB or more, or `exit()` on failure | Large allocations (Substrate) |
| Pixmaps, clip masks, a logo image | Images (Maze) |
| A hack that restarts itself | Restart leak test (Maze, Substrate) |
| A `free` that relies on state `draw` sets up (a lazy `initted`) | Stopping before the first draw (Blaster) |
| Hairlines, fades or `glPolygonOffset` in a GL hack | Thin lines in a GL hack |
| Threads, GL, Xft, shared memory | Skipping a hack |
| A licence header | Read it; add a notices section only if it differs from jwz's |

## 2. Set up

Work in a worktree off `origin/main`. Its setup and the commands it refuses are
in "Worktree setup".

## 3. Red, copy, green

Follow `adding-a-hack.md`. Show the registry test failing before
copying. Fill each shim gap test-first, then break the code on purpose and
watch the test fail ("Tests that cannot be fooled"). Filling a missing
function is a shim gap. Changing what every hack sees (the runner, a default, a
shared helper) is not: stop and ask Rod first.

## 4. Verify on the host

Run `pio test -e native`, `uv run --with pytest --with pillow pytest tools/tests`
and `uv run tools/check_notices.py`, and dump frames at several counts. Host
frames cannot show a byte swap, which happens in the push to the display: judge
colour on the device, on a colour you know the answer to.

## 5. Device

Flash only after Rod says so in this conversation; approval for one flash is
not approval for the next. See "Device capture". Report "compiles", "host tests
pass" and "runs on the device" separately; only Rod can say what the screen
shows. If it is slow, measure, change one thing, flash again and compare; if it
is still slow, say so and suggest dropping it. Record the numbers in
`tools/assessment_measured.md`, marking anything unmeasured as such.

## 6. Deliver

Commit named paths. Open the draft PR with `entire trail create` and put what
is unverified in its body. After a rebase, a push needs `--force-with-lease`:
ask Rod each time. Rod approves and merges; then delete the branch and
fast-forward `main`. New gotchas go in the matching `.claude/rules/` file (or
`AGENTS.md` if they apply everywhere) in the same PR, and deferred
ideas become issues.

## Red flags

| Thought | Reality |
| --- | --- |
| "It is rated S, so I need not read it" | Maze was rated L for Xlib gaps; the real blocker was a 20 MB `calloc`. |
| "It compiles, so it works" | Rorschach compiled and rebooted on its first frame. |

The `port-hack` skill orders this work, says what to read for before copying a
hack, and holds a recipe per trap. The steps:

1. Check its row in `docs/porting-assessment.md` (effort and Speed band) and
   read its licence header.
2. Update the expected list in `firmware/test/test_hacks/test_hacks.c` and see
   it fail.
3. Copy the file to `firmware/src/hacks/<name>/<name>.c`, add the notices row
   and an `extern` plus entry in `hacks/registry.c`.
4. Fill shim gaps test-first in `firmware/test/test_xshim/`. The compile
   check in `score_hacks.py` shows what is missing.
5. Host tests pass, dump a frame and look at it, then (with Rod's go-ahead)
   flash and measure fps and free heap/PSRAM over serial. To pin its frame
   hash after looking at the frame, put `0x1ull` in `kBaseline`, run
   `pio test -e native -f test_hacks`, convert the "Was N" in the failure line
   with `python3 -c "print(hex(N))"`, and run it again.

    return "copyright" in head and any(p in head for p in NOTICE_PHRASES)

        (src_dir / "xs_support").rglob("*")
    )

        if path.suffix not in SUFFIXES or not path.is_file():

        rel = path.relative_to(src_dir)
